summary:
RENDER-SIDE SWEEP: what makes foliage photoreal, given good assets. Research only. Nothing was downloaded, bought, installed or edited. I read Landscape3D.tsx, foliageLighting.ts, photoMaterials.ts, renderPipeline.tsx, sceneLook.ts, Sky3D.tsx, PhotoTracer.tsx, photoEngine.ts, pcssShadows.ts and renderQuality.ts in .claude/worktrees/foundation-reveal. I also read three 0.185.1 and three-gpu-pathtracer 0.0.27 in its node_modules, plus render/sources/procedural.result.json and the web sources cited below. Millisecond figures are ESTIMATES, not measurements; the P0 harness's EXT_disjoint_timer_query_webgl2 probe should measure them.

BOTTOM LINE
1. Today's look is held back mainly by assets and three render bugs: the A2C alpha leak, dead translucency terms, and an effective leaf roughness of 0.26. The renderer itself has most of the right building blocks: MSAA plus A2C, GTAO, a cached 4096 sun shadow map, PCSS in showcase, HDRI image-based lighting, and a path tracer with MIS.
2. With good assets plus the live upgrades below, a desktop GPU can reach Twinmotion/Enscape real-time quality. A still frame at the Corner camera could then pass a casual glance.
3. Phones top out at a good-quality 3D render, never a photo.
4. Photo-mode stills are the only place a homeowner may be unable to tell a render from a photo. That needs the leaf emissive hack replaced by real transmission. It ideally also needs the WebGPU tracer, for instancing, native-resolution textures and the OIDN denoiser.

CAMERA SCALE (fov 38, so the view height is 0.689 x distance; in/px = 0.689 x D / H_px)
- 1600x900 at DPR 1.5 (H = 1350 px):
  - Bed close-up (about 10.6 ft): about 0.065 in/px.
  - Plant base macro / Tree in lawn (4-5 ft): about 0.025-0.03 in/px.
  - Front (assumed about 25 ft; the code gives no distance): about 0.15 in/px.
  - Corner (60-120 ft): 0.37-0.73 in/px.
- At Corner a 15 ft maple is about 250-370 px tall, a 24 in boxwood about 33-50 px, a 3 in leaf 4-8 px, and needles are sub-pixel.
- On a phone (balanced DPR 1.25, about 600 px canvas height, estimated) every footprint is about 2.25x larger, so leaves are sub-pixel.
- So at Corner, photorealism is decided by canopy-scale cues, not leaf texture: silhouette and porosity, the value split between sunlit and shaded foliage, colour, sun penumbra and dapple, contact darkening, and no shimmer. Leaf-level texture and geometry matter only at Front, Bed close-up and the macro cameras.

WHAT DECKCRAFT HAS AND WHAT IS MISSING, PER TOPIC (with cost)

1. Translucency and transmission
- Live view: MISSING in effect. foliageLighting.ts:30-41 adds leafBack and shade fill before opaque_fragment. outgoingLight is already summed by then (meshphysical.glsl.js:193-198), so neither term renders (render.result).
- Photo mode: fakes it with a shadow-unaware emissive glow (photoMaterials.ts:183-189, 422-436), so the two disagree.
- Physics: leaves reflect about 15% at the 550 nm green peak and absorb about 75%, leaving about 10% transmittance. Transmitted light is more yellow-green than reflected light (see the leaf-optics sources in route 1).
- Fix: a diffuse-transmission lobe, T·albedo_t·max(0, -N·L)·shadow/π for the sun plus a small irradiance term from -N, scaled by baked thickness/AO. Inject it before totalDiffuse.
- Cost: about 1-1.5 KB gzip in the lazy Landscape3D chunk, plus 2 B/vertex for AO and thickness. GPU estimate +0.1-0.3 ms on desktop at 3.2 MP and +0.3-1 ms on a phone.
- three 0.185 has no KHR_materials_diffuse_transmission. I grepped src and examples and found nothing; Babylon 8 does support it.

2. Leaf specular
- PARTLY there but wrong. roughness = min(r, 0.64) multiplied by the map's G channel (about 0.40) gives about 0.26 effective, which produces sky glints.
- Normal maps sit on minified cards, with no geometric specular AA.
- With DoubleSide, three flips back-face normals (normal_fragment_begin.glsl.js:16), so canopies shade card by card.
- There is no aoMap, so specular occlusion (aomap_fragment.glsl.js:21) never applies inside canopies.
- Target: F0 0.04 (IOR 1.5); upper side roughness about 0.5-0.65, under side about 0.7-0.85. Bake Toksvig/LEAN roughness into mips, or use Valve/Tokuyoshi geometric specular AA. Use baked AO for specular occlusion.
- Cost: 0 bytes; under 0.05 ms.

3. Normal-mapped and bent normals
- MISSING. Transfer crown or proxy-sphere normals onto the card vertices, blended 50-80% with the card normals, and stop the back-face flip for leaf cards.
- Cost: 0 bytes if the normals are replaced, or +4 B/vertex (octahedral) if both are kept. 0 ms.

4. AO and contact shadows
- HAS: GTAO at half resolution with 16 samples, blended at 0.5 by day.
- HAS: a ground-occlusion map, but only for lawn and hardscape, not beds.
- MISSING: baked canopy AO, an occlusion map for beds, and a contact cue on the constrained tier (no plant shadows there).
- Cost:
  - Base contact decals: one instanced draw, about 0.05 ms.
  - Bed aoMap: about 0 ms.
  - Vertex AO: 1 B/vertex.

5. Shadow softness
- Editor shadows are PCF: 5 Vogel compare taps. PCSS (8 blocker + 8 filter taps) runs only in showcase post (pcssShadows.ts).
- The shadow map is cached (shadowCache), so it costs 0 ms per frame when static.
- Shadow texel size is frustum width / map size. A 150 ft frustum gives 0.44 in at 4096, 0.88 in at 2048 and 1.76 in at 1024. Leaf-scale dapple therefore exists only on the high tier.
- The photo-mode sun radius is 0.9 deg by day (photoGrade.ts:26). The real sun is about 0.265 deg (0.53 deg diameter), so penumbrae and sun flecks are about 3.4x too soft.
- The real penumbra is about 0.0093 x the occluder-to-receiver distance: about 1.1 in under a 10 ft canopy.
- PCSS costs about +11 fetches per lit fragment against PCF: an estimated +0.3-1 ms on desktop and +1-3 ms on a phone.
- Also: three's shadow depth for A2C materials uses a fixed alphaTest of 0.5 (WebGLShadowMap.js:482), while the visible cutoff is 0.3-0.4. Plant shadows are therefore thinner than the canopy that casts them. A customDepthMaterial fixes it at 0 cost.

6. Alpha antialiasing
- HAS: A2C with MSAA 4 on high and 2 on balanced (Landscape3D.tsx:57). three's alphatest chunk already sharpens alpha with smoothstep(alphaTest, alphaTest + fwidth). That is Golus-style A2C.
- BUG: alpha below 1 leaks to the canvas (alpha:true). The fix is planned: canvas alpha:false.
- MISSING:
  - Coverage-preserving mips. WebGL box-filters mips, so 55%-coverage maple atlases go blobby and 25%-coverage needle atlases vanish (Castaño). Building them offline costs 0 ms at runtime.
  - A mip-level alpha scale (about 4 ALU ops).
  - A constrained-tier answer (MSAA 0 there): alphaHash (Wyman) or idle accumulation.
  - Any temporal accumulation in the live view. SHOWCASE_STILL_SAMPLES = 1, so the jitter-and-blend code in renderPipeline.tsx:75-84 never runs. Reusing it when the camera goes idle (8-16 jittered frames) costs about 0.05-0.1 s on desktop and 0.2-0.4 s on a phone, plus about 52 MB for two half-float targets on the high tier. It removes shimmer, PCSS and GTAO noise, and A2C quantisation (4x MSAA has only 5 coverage levels).
- WebGL2 resolves MSAA in linear HDR before tone mapping. Renderbuffers cannot be custom-resolved in WebGL2. Leaf edges against a bright sky therefore look thinned. Idle accumulation should weight samples in tone-mapped space (Karis 1/(1+luma)); WebGPU allows a proper resolve.

7. Leaf density and silhouette
- Today's shrub cards are about 12x real leaf size.
- LOD1 and LOD2 drop cards without enlarging the rest.
- The showcase estate has 2.52M triangles; the plan takes it to 0.84M.
- Needed:
  - True-size twig-cluster cards.
  - Species crown envelopes with real porosity: 10-30% sky gaps for deciduous crowns, about 0 for clipped evergreens.
  - Opaque leaf meshes for hosta, daylily, grasses and hero perennials.
  - LOD2 as a billboard cloud or octahedral impostor.
- Suggested LOD0 budgets: canopy tree 40-120k triangles, shrub 10-40k, perennial 3-15k, grass 3-8k. That puts 273 plants at roughly 5-10M triangles: showcase on desktop only. Balanced LOD1 stays within the existing 120k extra-triangle budget, which means card clouds on phones.

8. Texture resolution per LOD
- Targets:
  - LOD0: 16-32 texels/in on leaves. A 2048 atlas per leaf family; 4096 or per-leaf 256 px sprites for the macro cameras.
  - LOD1: 4-8 texels/in (1024).
  - LOD2: 1-2 texels/in (512), or a 2048 octahedral impostor sheet.
- Bytes per map:
  - RGBA8 with mips: 22.4 MB at 2048, 5.6 MB at 1024, 1.4 MB at 512.
  - UASTC transcoded to BC7/ASTC: 5.6 MB at 2048. ETC1S to BC1/ETC1: about 2.8 MB.
  - Four leaf-family atlases with two maps each at 2048 come to 179 MB as RGBA8, against about 45 MB compressed. KTX2 is therefore mandatory for showcase LOD0.
- Measured here: basis_transcoder.wasm 527,333 B (245,397 B gzip); basis_transcoder.js 57,529 B (15,084 B gzip); KTX2Loader.js 36,567 B (about 9 KB gzip, unminified).
- The WebGL path tracer resamples EVERY scene texture to a 1024x1024 RGBA8 layer with no mips: 4 MB per layer (WebGLPathTracer.js:142, :233; RenderTarget2DArray generateMipmaps:false).

9. Colour grading against photos
- HAS:
  - Neutral tone mapping at exposure 1 in the live view.
  - A showcase grade: CDL-style slope/offset/power, contrast 1.1, split tone, vignette 0.1.
  - AgX in the photo blit only, so the live view and photos already render greens differently.
  - A pow(0.8) albedo lift plus green gain, which brightens leaves by about 21-37%.
- MISSING: any calibration loop.
- Needed:
  - A ColorChecker in RAW reference photos of each species under midsummer sun.
  - A virtual ColorChecker in the scene.
  - Per-species colour within ΔE2000 of about 5 of the photo means.
  - Summer-foliage linear albedo of about 0.09-0.12 (sRGB about 60-100 green).
  - Per-plant variation of about 2-4 ΔE.
  - A phone-camera-like curve (S-curve plus highlight roll-off) for Realistic look and Photo mode, with Neutral kept for editor swatches.
- Runtime cost 0. Hardware: Calibrite ColorChecker Classic US$74.25 on sale (US$99 list).

PHOTO MODE (three-gpu-pathtracer 0.0.27, WebGLPathTracer)
What it already does well:
- MIS between light and BSDF sampling, with a circular RectAreaLight sun (MIS-sampled) and HDRI environment importance sampling.
- 5 bounces, 6 transmissive bounces, filterGlossy 0.55.
- Per-sample hard alpha test, so no A2C is needed: pixel jitter antialiases.
- DoubleSide cards and true multi-bounce GI: green bounce, sky occlusion under canopies, real contact shading.

What it cannot do:
- No diffuse-transmission or SSS lobe. Thin-wall transmission (thickness 0, MaterialsTexture.js:329) is specular refraction blurred by roughness, coloured with the same albedo as reflection.
- Shadow rays do pass stochastically through transmissive leaves with an albedo tint (attenuate_hit_function.glsl.js:125-147). So thin-wall transmission of 0.1-0.25 at roughness about 0.6 gives real, shadow-aware light through stacked leaves.
- Emissive surfaces get no MIS (README).
- Alpha skips eat the transmissive budget, then regular bounces (PhysicalPathTracingMaterial.js:464-465). Shadow rays that run out count as blocked, so dense canopies go too dark.
- There is no instancing: DeckCraft bakes every instance into one world-space mesh (bakeInstances). Memory is roughly 70-100 B per triangle (estimate), so about 0.5-0.7 GB for 7M triangles.
- Textures are capped at 1024.
- The WebGL path was deprecated in 0.0.25 (2026-09-28) and will be removed in a future release.

What it needs:
1. Drop the emissive leaf glow and the albedo lift.
2. Use thin-wall transmission, or better a roughly 50-line GLSL patch adding a Lambertian transmission lobe, keyed on thin-film plus roughness of at least 0.5 so glass stays specular.
3. Transmissive bounces 10-16 for foliage.
4. Sun radius 0.265 deg.
5. OIDN with albedo and normal AOVs; the batch path already has it.
6. textureSize 2048 for close-up stills only (16 MB per layer).
7. Better still, port to WebGPUPathTracer. It has per-instance BVH (InstancedMesh and BatchedMesh), native-resolution atlas pages, maxTransparentBounces 5 kept separate from maxBounces 15 for foliage, an in-browser OIDNDenoiser, an FSR upscaler and SunLight. It also lacks diffuse transmission and would need the same patch in WGSL.

Realistic Photo-mode result with good assets:
- Archviz-still quality (Corona/V-Ray class) at Corner and Front.
- Bed close-up and macro limited by card leaves and the 1024 texture cap on WebGL.
- Corner pass-as-photo is achievable.

BEST PHOTOREAL VEGETATION ON THE WEB (what each does)
- Sketchfab viewer (WebGL PBR, with translucency and SSS channels since 2017, https://sketchfab.com/blogs/community/sketchfab-now-supports-subsurface-scattering-translucency):
  - ffishAsia CC0 plant scans (https://sketchfab.com/ffishAsia-and-floraZia): 200k-2.8M faces, 15-225 MB each.
  - e-on PlantCatalog (https://sketchfab.com/PlantCatalog).
  - These are the most photoreal close-up leaves in WebGL, but as single heavy hero objects under IBL, not lit scenes.
- Babylon.js 8 diffuse-transmission houseplant (https://aka.ms/babylon8gltfdemo, listed at https://babylonjs.com/featureDemos/), using the Khronos DiffuseTransmissionPlant sample (https://github.com/KhronosGroup/glTF-Sample-Assets/blob/main/Models/DiffuseTransmissionPlant/README.md, CC BY 4.0 materials). It shows a real-time diffuse-transmission lobe; the extension is a Release Candidate (https://github.com/KhronosGroup/glTF/blob/main/extensions/2.0/Khronos/KHR_materials_diffuse_transmission/README.md).
- three.js:
  - agargaro octahedral-impostor forest (https://octahedral-impostor.vercel.app, https://github.com/agargaro/octahedral-impostor): 200k trees using InstancedMesh2, meshoptimizer LODs and 16x16, 2048 px hemi-octahedral impostors. A template for phone LOD2.
  - EZ-Tree (https://tympanus.net/codrops/2025/01/27/fractals-to-forests-creating-realistic-3d-trees-with-three-js/): good procedural skeletons, card foliage, not photoreal close up.
  - The WebGPU SSGI/TRAA examples (https://threejs.org/examples/webgpu_postprocessing_ssgi.html) run on WebGPURenderer only.
- PlayCanvas and Spark Gaussian splats (https://blog.playcanvas.com/playcanvas-open-sources-sog-format-for-gaussian-splatting/; SplatGarden on Spark + three.js with about 3M splats, https://omolism.cargo.site/SplatGarden; flora captures, https://nebulousflynn.substack.com/p/3d-gaussian-splats-of-local-flora). These are captured, so they are the most photographic plants in a browser. But the lighting is baked: no relighting, no cast shadows, and about 10-25 MB per million splats.
- Unreal Pixel Streaming:
  - Twinmotion Cloud Presentations (https://dev.epicgames.com/documentation/en-us/twinmotion/an-overview-of-twinmotion-cloud): Ultra quality, 60-minute session cap, textures up to 2K, 100 concurrent viewers.
  - UE 5.7 Nanite Foliage is experimental; Epic claims realistic foliage at 60 FPS (https://80.lv/articles/unreal-engine-5-7-is-now-availabe).
  - This is the highest live realism, paid per minute.
- Enscape Web Standalone (https://learn.enscape3d.com/?p=64153): WebGL2, capped at Draft quality, grass material disabled, no Safari or iOS support. Even archviz vendors downgrade vegetation for the browser.
- Lumion: 'LiveSync for Web' and Lumion Cloud were reported only by secondary sources (unverified).
- Structure Studios VizTerra v4 (April 2026, desktop, path tracing; https://www.structurestudios.com/vizterra) is the landscape-software quality bar, but not on the web.

REALISTIC CEILINGS
(a) Live view on a phone
- Balanced: LOD1, MSAA 2, DPR 1.25, 2048 shadow map. Constrained: LOD2, no MSAA, no plant shadows.
- The ceiling is a clean, well-lit 3D model: species-correct card clouds or impostors, translucency, contact decals, coverage-preserving mips, and idle accumulation for still frames.
- About 6/10 at Corner when still and 4-5/10 while orbiting. Obviously CG at Bed close-up.
- Never indistinguishable from a photo.

(b) Live view on a desktop GPU
- High or showcase: LOD0/LOD1, PCSS, A2C 4x, translucency, crown normals, vertex AO, calibrated colour, idle 16-sample accumulation, and a phone-camera grade.
- Twinmotion/Enscape real-time class: about 7-8/10 at Corner when still. A small (1080p or lower) still might pass a casual homeowner if the house, lawn and sky are equally good.
- Front and Bed close-up still read as CG: flat cards, sprite repetition, no GI under shrubs (unless the renderer moves to WebGPU SSGI).

(c) Photo-mode stills
- With the fixes on the current WebGL tracer: about 8-9/10 at Corner and Front, 7-8/10 at macro.
- With the WebGPU tracer plus diffuse transmission and native-resolution atlases: about 9/10.
- With server-side Cycles and scan-grade assets: about 9-9.5/10.

WHAT 'INDISTINGUISHABLE FROM A PHOTO' MEANS AT CORNER (proposed gates)
1. Silhouette porosity and edge raggedness within ±10% of species reference photos at equal pixel height.
2. Sunlit-to-shaded foliage luminance about 4-10x, with near-black interior pockets.
3. Mean sunlit-leaf colour within ΔE2000 of about 5 of calibrated photos, plus 2-4 ΔE variation per plant.
4. Sun penumbra consistent with a 0.53 deg sun, dappled light under trees, and darkened plant bases.
5. Zero shimmer and no LOD pops in the presented frame (8 or more accumulated samples).
6. Plants seated in mulch (no burial, no float).
7. House, lawn and sky at the same realism.
8. In a blind test (owner plus 5-10 homeowners, 10 render/photo crop pairs at Corner), no better than 60% correct identification.
- Photo mode can meet this. Desktop live is borderline, on a still frame only. Phones cannot.

PRICES FOUND
- Calibrite ColorChecker Classic: US$74.25 sale / US$99 list (https://calibrite.com/us/product/colorchecker-classic/).
- Epson Perfection V39 II scanner: US$129.99 MSRP (SHI listing); Walmart.ca shows C$327.28.
- RunPod: RTX 4090 at $0.34/h community or $0.89/h secure, $1.10/h serverless; L4 at $0.44-0.59/h (https://www.runpod.io/pricing).
- Arcware: Lite €10/month + €0.15/min; Core €89/month + up to €0.10/min (https://arcware.com/pricing/).
- Vagon Streams: $0.025-0.047/min plus $0.67/day per app (https://vagon.io/streams/pricing).
- Twinmotion seat: $445/year (secondary source: visualizee.ai).
- Every purchase or sign-up needs owner approval.

routes.name: R1 Live foliage shader v2: translucency, two-sided specular, crown/bent normals, baked canopy AO and thickness
routes.what:
Replace foliage-summer-v1 (foliageLighting.ts). Its translucency and shade-fill terms are inserted after outgoingLight is summed (meshphysical.glsl.js:193-198), so they never render.

The new patch injects at #include <aomap_fragment>, before totalDiffuse:
(1) Diffuse transmission. Sun term T·albedo_t·max(0,-N·L)·shadow/π, plus a small irradiance term from -N. Scale both by baked thickness/AO.
(2) Upper-side roughness 0.5-0.65 and under-side 0.7-0.85, F0 0.04. Today min(r,.64)×map.G gives about 0.26, which means glints.
(3) Crown/proxy-sphere normals blended 50-80% into the card normals. Do not flip leaf-card back-face normals; three does that at normal_fragment_begin.glsl.js:16.
(4) A per-vertex AO attribute feeding specular occlusion. computeSpecularOcclusion only runs with an aoMap (aomap_fragment.glsl.js:21).
(5) Geometric specular AA (Valve/Tokuyoshi), or Toksvig roughness baked into mips.
(6) Remove the pow(0.8) albedo lift and the green gain.

The same parameters must drive Photo mode.
routes.species_coverage:
Technique that applies to all 26 species.
- Biggest gain: broadleaf species seen backlit (sugar maple, red maple, redbud, serviceberry, both hydrangeas, ninebark, dogwood, lilac, hosta, ostrich fern, daylily) and the three grasses, which glow when backlit.
- Smaller gain: needle and scale-leaf species (pine, blue spruce, Smaragd, yew, boxwood). For them use low transmission (about 0.03-0.06) and mainly AO plus crown normals.
routes.realism:
This is the largest live-view lever once assets are right. Canopies shade as volumes, not faceted cards. Backlit leaves glow yellow-green at golden hour. Shaded sides stay green instead of black, and leaves look matte with a soft sheen.

Physics anchors:
- About 15% reflectance at the 550 nm green peak (https://sites.bu.edu/cliveg/files/2023/10/leaf-optics-jacquemoud-ustin.pdf, and the classic measurements found via search).
- About 75% absorptance at 550 nm (PMC10033640, as quoted in a search summary; page not readable), so transmittance is about 10%.
- Summer foliage linear albedo about 0.09-0.12 (community chart, https://polycount.com/discussion/comment/2085603).
- Grass albedo (0.105, 0.133, 0.041) (https://physicallybased.info/).

Industry references:
- UE Two Sided Foliage: subsurface colour sets transmission (https://dev.epicgames.com/documentation/en-us/unreal-engine/shading-models-in-unreal-engine).
- Crysis per-vertex translucency and back-lighting (https://developer.nvidia.com/gpugems/gpugems3/part-iii-rendering/chapter-16-vegetation-procedural-animation-and-shading-crysis).
- Habel et al. 2007, physically based real-time leaf translucency (https://cg.tuwien.ac.at/research/publications/2007/Habel_2007_RTT).

routes.cost:
$0 cash.

Bytes:
- About 1-1.5 KB gzip in the lazy Landscape3D chunk, not the budgeted 340 KB viewer chunk.
- AO plus thickness as two normalized Uint8 vertex attributes: 2 B/vertex (about 130 KB raw for a 65k-vertex tree before meshopt).
- Crown normals replace normals (0 B), or add 4 B/vertex if octahedral normals are kept alongside.

GPU (ESTIMATE): +0.1-0.3 ms on a desktop at about 3.2 MP with plants on about 40% of pixels at overdraw 3; +0.3-1 ms on a phone. To be measured with the P0 harness.
routes.owner_actions:
1. Decide plan question D2 (make the terms live, physically scaled).
2. Sign off before/after look pairs at Corner, Front and Bed close-up, day and golden hour.
3. Accept that Photo mode changes to match.
routes.web_fit:
Pure shader and vertex-attribute work, in the lazy chunk.
- Works on every tier. On constrained (no plant shadows) the transmission must be gated by AO only, not by the shadow map.
- Needs per-vertex AO, thickness and crown-normal attributes baked by the asset build (GLTFLoader passes custom attributes through lower-cased).
- No texture-size change. A thickness map can be packed into the normal map's B channel or the roughness map's spare channel, at 0 extra bytes.
routes.risks:
1. Unshadowed translucency turns beds neon. photoMaterials.ts already notes this happened. Transmission must be multiplied by the sun shadow and divided by π.
2. Neutral tone mapping makes saturated backlit greens look plastic. Pair this with route R6.
3. Every change must be mirrored in photoMaterials.ts or the live view and Photo mode diverge again.
4. Crown normals done naively (pure radial) look bad, per the Houdini forum (https://www.sidefx.com/forum/post/409260/). Blend them with the card normals.

routes.name: R2 Alpha pipeline and antialiasing: A2C fix, coverage-preserving mips, mip alpha scale, hashed alpha, idle progressive supersampling
routes.what:
Keep alpha-to-coverage, which DeckCraft already uses with MSAA 4 on high and 2 on balanced. three's alphatest chunk already sharpens alpha with smoothstep(alphaTest, alphaTest+fwidth(a), a), the Golus approach. Then add:
(1) Canvas alpha:false, already planned, to stop alpha below 1 reaching the page.
(2) Coverage-preserving mipmaps built offline. Per mip, find the reference value that preserves the base coverage by bisection, then scale alpha (Castaño, http://www.ludicon.com/castano/blog/articles/computing-alpha-mipmaps/). WebGL box-filters today, so 55%-coverage maple atlases go blobby and 25% needle atlases vanish.
(3) Optionally a shader mip-level alpha scale (Golus, https://bgolus.medium.com/anti-aliased-alpha-test-the-esoteric-alpha-to-coverage-8b177335ae4f).
(4) Constrained tier (MSAA 0): three's Material.alphaHash (hashed alpha testing, https://research.nvidia.com/labs/rtr/publication/wyman2017hashed), only together with accumulation.
(5) Idle progressive supersampling in the live view. frameloop is demand-driven, so after the camera stops, render 8-16 sub-pixel-jittered frames and blend them. Reuse jitterCamera and the blend pass in renderPipeline.tsx:75-84, which never runs today because SHOWCASE_STILL_SAMPLES=1. Weight samples in tone-mapped space (Karis 1/(1+luma)).
(6) Give plant shadows a customDepthMaterial with the visible cutoff. three forces alphaTest 0.5 for A2C materials in the shadow pass (WebGLShadowMap.js:482), against the visible 0.3-0.4.
routes.species_coverage:
All 26.
- Critical for needle and scale species (white pine, blue spruce, Smaragd, yew, boxwood), whose atlases sit near or below the cutoff and vanish at distance.
- Critical for fine grasses (Karl Foerster, little bluestem, switchgrass), which shimmer most.
routes.realism:
Shimmer and crawl while orbiting are the strongest CG giveaway at Corner, where leaves are 1-8 px. There is no temporal antialiasing in the live view today.

Idle accumulation gives every tier a supersampled still. That includes constrained phones with no MSAA, and it also cleans PCSS and GTAO noise. 4x MSAA alone gives only 5 coverage levels; 8 jittered frames give about 40.

Coverage-preserving mips keep canopy density at distance.

Limit: WebGL2 resolves MSAA renderbuffers in linear HDR before tone mapping, and it has no multisample textures for a custom resolve. Leaf edges against a bright sky therefore read thinned. Tone-mapped accumulation mitigates this; WebGPU can fix it. On HDR plus MSAA see https://discourse.threejs.org/t/having-geometric-specular-antialiasing-would-be-incredible/74816.
routes.licence:
Techniques, plus three.js MIT (quoted in R1) for the alphaHash and A2C paths already in core.

No third-party code is required. The Castaño and Golus articles describe methods; nothing is copied.
routes.cost:
$0.

Runtime:
- Offline coverage mips: 0 ms. A runtime canvas rebuild of mips at load would cost an estimated 5-30 ms CPU per 1-2k atlas.
- Mip alpha scale: about 4 ALU per fragment.
- Idle accumulation runs only when the camera stops. ESTIMATE: 8 extra frames at 6-12 ms on desktop is 0.05-0.1 s; on a phone, 25-50 ms each is 0.2-0.4 s.

Memory: two extra half-float targets, about 52 MB at 2400x1350 (high tier) and about 5 MB on a phone canvas.

A2C/MSAA is already paid for.
routes.owner_actions:
1. Approve idle accumulation as visible behaviour: the image refines for under half a second after the camera stops.
2. Approve the canvas alpha:false change, already in plan P0.
routes.web_fit:
Offline mip chains require KTX2 (see R4) or a mip-chain bake.
- The accumulation code already exists in renderPipeline.tsx/showcasePost; it is lazy-loaded.
- Works on all tiers.
- On a phone, cap at 8 samples and keep DPR at 1-1.25.
routes.risks:
1. Accumulation must reset on any invalidate (data edit, LOD change, sky change), or it ghosts.
2. Phone thermals if users keep nudging the camera: cap the samples.
3. alphaHash without accumulation looks noisy.
4. On tile-based GPUs, alpha-tested geometry defeats early depth and hidden-surface removal. A11+ Apple GPUs improve discard cost (https://developer.apple.com/tutorials/data/documentation/metal/tailor-your-apps-for-apple-gpus-and-tile-based-deferred-rendering.md), but PowerVR advises against discard (https://docs.imgtec.com/starter-guides/powervr-architecture/html/topics/rules/do-not-use-discard.html). Profile on the owner's iPhone.

routes.name: R3 Shadows and grounding: PCSS sized to the real sun, shadow texel budget, contact decals, bed occlusion, canopy AO
routes.what:
Shadows: DeckCraft has a cached, fitted sun shadow map (4096/2048/1024 by tier) and GTAO at half resolution. PCSS (8 blocker + 8 filter taps, pcssShadows.ts) runs only in showcase post; the editor uses three's 5-tap Vogel PCF.

Changes:
(1) Size the PCSS light to the real sun. Its angular diameter is about 0.53 deg (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Angular_diameter), so penumbra ≈ 0.0093 × the occluder-to-receiver distance: about 1.1 in under a 10 ft canopy, sharp at stems. Enable PCSS for Realistic look on the high tier.
(2) Photo-mode sun radius 0.265 deg instead of 0.9 deg (photoGrade.ts:26). Today's value makes penumbrae and sun flecks about 3.4x too soft.
(3) One InstancedMesh of radial contact decals under every plant, on all tiers. Constrained phones have no plant shadows.
(4) Feed the GroundOcclusion texture to bed materials, which today only the lawn and hardscape get, and let plants enter the occlusion cover pass at any LOD.
(5) Per-vertex canopy AO (see R1) on top of GTAO.
(6) Optionally LOD2 shadows on the high tier; the map is cached, so the cost is redraw-only.
routes.species_coverage:
All 26.
- Trees (sugar maple, red maple, redbud, serviceberry, white pine, blue spruce) gain dapple and penumbra.
- Low perennials, grasses and hosta gain most from contact darkening.
routes.realism:
At Corner scale the strongest 'it is a photo' cues are: sun shadows crisp at the base and soft and dappled further out; darkened plant bases; and the near-black interiors of shrubs. Over-soft shadows read as CG.

Shadow texel size = frustum width / map size. A 150 ft frustum gives 0.44 in at 4096, 0.88 in at 2048 and 1.76 in at 1024. Leaf-scale dapple is therefore only plausible on high/showcase; balanced shows canopy-scale shadows.
routes.licence: In-house code on three.js MIT (quoted in R1). The NVIDIA PCSS idea is a published technique with no code dependency.
routes.cost:
$0.

ESTIMATES:
- PCSS: about +11 texture fetches per sun-lit fragment against PCF, i.e. +0.3-1 ms on desktop at 3.2 MP and +1-3 ms on a phone. Keep it off on phones.
- Contact decals: 1 draw, about 0.05 ms, one 64-128 px canvas texture (under 70 KB GPU).
- Bed aoMap: about 0 ms; reuses the existing GroundOcclusion texture.
- Photo sun radius: 0 cost, and slightly less penumbra noise.
- Shadow map: unchanged memory (4096² depth is 64 MB at 32-bit), 0 ms per frame when static (shadowCache).
routes.owner_actions: Look sign-off: shadow crispness at the Corner, Tree in lawn and Plant base macro cameras, day and golden hour.
routes.web_fit: Runtime-only. No asset bytes beyond a tiny decal texture, so it fits every tier. PCSS stays gated to high/showcase.
routes.risks:
1. PCSS with 8+8 point taps is noisy in a single frame. It needs R2 idle accumulation, or more taps (more ms).
2. A sharper sun exposes shadow-map texel aliasing on balanced (2048).
3. Decals must sit on the bed finish height (plan fix for the 3.05 in burial), or they float or are hidden.

routes.name: R4 Texture resolution per LOD and GPU compression (KTX2 / Basis Universal)
routes.what:
A texel-density policy derived from the camera footprint, in/px = 0.689 × distance / drawing-buffer height (fov 38).

Footprints at 1600x900, DPR 1.5:
- Bed close-up: about 0.065 in/px.
- Plant base macro / Tree in lawn: about 0.025-0.03 in/px.
- Front (assumed 25 ft): about 0.15 in/px.
- Corner: 0.37-0.73 in/px.
- Phones: about 2.25x coarser.

Policy:
- LOD0: 16-32 texels per inch of leaf. A 2048 atlas per leaf family; 4096 or per-leaf 256 px sprites only for hero species seen at the macro cameras.
- LOD1: 4-8 texels/in, 1024.
- LOD2: 1-2 texels/in, 512, or a 2048 octahedral impostor sheet.

Ship as KTX2:
- UASTC (to BC7/ASTC 4x4) for albedo+alpha and for normal+thickness+roughness packed.
- ETC1S where quality allows.
- Load with three's KTX2Loader in the lazy chunk, with the transcoder as static files.
routes.species_coverage: All 26. Shared leaf-family atlases: broadleaf-small, broadleaf-large, needle/scale, grass and perennial plus flowers. Per-species atlases would multiply memory.
routes.realism: Prevents blurry close-ups (Bed close-up, macro) and wasted bytes at Corner. Without compression, photoreal LOD0 atlases cannot fit in browser GPU memory, so this is an enabler rather than a look.
routes.licence:
three.js KTX2Loader: MIT (quoted in R1).

Basis Universal transcoder (node_modules/three/examples/jsm/libs/basis): Apache-2.0 (https://github.com/BinomialLLC/basis_universal). The repo states 'All rights reserved except as granted under the Apache 2.0 LICENSE', and Apache-2.0 §2 grants a 'perpetual, worldwide, non-exclusive, no-charge, royalty-free, irrevocable copyright license to reproduce ... and distribute'.

Committing the transcoder to the public repo and serving it is allowed, with the NOTICE/licence kept.
routes.cost:
$0.

Measured from node_modules:
- basis_transcoder.wasm: 527,333 B (245,397 B gzip).
- basis_transcoder.js: 57,529 B (15,084 B gzip).
- KTX2Loader.js: 36,567 B (about 9,003 B gzip, unminified).

GPU per map with mips:
- RGBA8: 22.4 MB at 2048, 5.6 MB at 1024, 1.4 MB at 512.
- UASTC to BC7/ASTC: 5.6 / 1.4 / 0.35 MB.
- ETC1S to BC1/ETC1 (RGB): about half that.

Example: 4 families × 2 maps at 2048 is 179 MB as RGBA8 against about 45 MB compressed.

Download: file sizes depend on content. Rule of thumb, unverified: ETC1S about 0.5-1.5 MB per 2048 map, UASTC+RDO+zstd about 2-4 MB. Measure on real atlases.

Transcode CPU time is not measured; it runs in a worker.
routes.owner_actions: Approve adding the transcoder static files (about 260 KB gzip, fetched only when plants load) and the build-time KTX2 encoding step. The encoder is a dev tool: the basisu CLI (Apache-2.0) or gltf-transform.
routes.web_fit:
- Phones never load LOD0: balanced is at most LOD1 (1024 atlases), constrained is LOD2 (512 or impostor).
- Showcase LOD0 (273 plants) needs about 45-60 MB of compressed leaf atlases, which is desktop-only.
- Also needed: per-mip coverage-preserving alpha (R2) baked into the KTX2 mip chain.
- Photo mode: the WebGL tracer resamples every texture to a 1024² RGBA8 layer with no mips (WebGLPathTracer.js:142, :233; RenderTarget2DArray generateMipmaps:false), 4 MB per layer. KTX2 textures would need decoding or uncompressed copies for the tracer.
routes.risks:
1. KTX2 textures are compressed GPU formats. The WebGL path tracer cannot read them directly, so Photo mode needs a separate uncompressed source (CPU-side or re-fetch); budget memory and time for that.
2. iOS and Android pick different targets (ASTC/ETC2), so quality must be checked on the owner's iPhone.
3. A 4096 hero atlas on the high tier must be guarded by the maxTextureSize capability.

routes.name: R5 Leaf density and silhouette: geometry policy and LOD scheme
routes.what:
Build plants so their silhouette and porosity match the species at every LOD:
- True-size twig-cluster cards: leaf length × cluster size, not a fraction of the envelope as today, where shrub cards are about 12x real leaf size.
- Card count = shell area / (card area × coverage).
- Species crown envelopes with sky gaps: about 10-30% porosity for deciduous crowns, about 0 for clipped Smaragd/boxwood/yew, using hull plus shell.
- Opaque, non-alpha leaf meshes for hosta, daylily, grass blades and hero perennial heads.
- LOD1 enlarges the retained cards by sqrt(1/retention), so silhouette is preserved.
- LOD2 is a billboard cloud or an octahedral impostor (16x16 views, 2048, hemi-octahedron, as in agargaro's three.js forest: https://octahedral-impostor.vercel.app, https://github.com/agargaro/octahedral-impostor).
- Uniform or XZ-isotropic scaling, so leaves do not stretch.
routes.species_coverage:
All 26:
- Trees (5): space-colonisation or ez-tree skeletons plus cluster cards.
- Clipped and needle evergreens (Smaragd, boxwood, yew, blue spruce, white pine): hull plus shell, needle sprays.
- Broadleaf shrubs (ninebark, red-osier dogwood, both hydrangeas, spirea, lilac): cluster cards.
- Perennials and grasses (coneflower, black-eyed Susan, bergamot, hosta, ostrich fern, daylily, catmint, salvia, three grasses): opaque blades and leaves.
routes.realism:
At Corner the eye reads crown shape, porosity, clumping and the scale of leaf masses. Wrong leaf size or a solid blob is an instant CG tell, and so is thinning at distance.

Opaque leaf meshes remove alpha edge artefacts entirely at Bed close-up and macro, where cards betray themselves.
routes.licence:
In-house generators (procedural.result recommends an in-repo space-colonisation build).

ez-tree is MIT per procedural.result. The agargaro impostor demo's licence was not stated on the forum post, so only re-implement the technique. Card textures come from whatever asset route other sweeps choose.
routes.cost:
$0 cash.

Suggested LOD0 budgets:
- Canopy tree 40-120k triangles.
- Shrub 10-40k.
- Perennial 3-15k.
- Grass 3-8k.

That gives the 273-plant showcase about 5-10M triangles, against 2.52M today and the plan's 0.84M. ESTIMATE: desktop draw plus shadow at about 4-10 ms. Desktop only.

LOD1 at about 25% of LOD0; the balanced tier keeps the existing 120k extra-triangle budget. LOD2 at 1-2k or a 2-triangle impostor.

Alpha-card overdraw is about 2-4x on plant pixels.

Geometry bytes: about 12-20 B per triangle after meshopt quantisation (estimate), so a 30k-triangle shrub is about 0.4-0.6 MB per LOD0 file.
routes.owner_actions:
1. Choose the triangle budget for Realistic look on desktop.
2. Accept that Realistic look stays desktop-oriented. On phones the showcase force-LOD0 rule (273 plants) would exceed memory, so LOD0 should be clamped to near plants or the frustum on phones.
routes.web_fit:
- GLB per species per LOD.
- Shared leaf-family atlases (R4).
- BatchedMesh per form plus LOD to keep draw calls bounded (three core).
- Impostor atlases at 2048 per species group for phones.
- Effort: offline build scripts plus the render-time species map (already in plan P3+).
routes.risks:
1. Showcase force-LOD0 on 273 plants with photoreal budgets may break the per-frame budget and the photo-mode BVH memory (R7). Consider frustum- or distance-clamped LOD0 even in showcase.
2. Octahedral impostors cannot be relit for time of day unless normal and depth are baked as well; they also need relighting in the shader.

routes.name: R6 Colour calibration against photos and a photographic grade
routes.what:
Set leaf albedo and the tone pipeline from measurements:
(1) The owner shoots RAW reference photos of each species (jobs or nursery) with a ColorChecker in frame, under midsummer sun at about 2 pm, plus a backlit shot.
(2) Extract linear sunlit-leaf colour relative to the chart's neutral patches.
(3) Optionally use flatbed scans of real leaves: reflective for albedo; a light box or backlit scan for transmission colour and thickness masks. These are owner-made, so there is no licence issue.
(4) Render a virtual ColorChecker in the scene to verify Neutral (live), the showcase grade and AgX (photo).
(5) Gate: per-species mean ΔE2000 of about 5 or less against the photo; 2-4 ΔE per-plant variation; seasonal variants (spring lime, summer deep, fall).
(6) Remove pow(0.8) and the green gains (foliageLighting.ts:27-29; photoMaterials.ts:139-180).
(7) Use a phone-camera-like curve (S-curve, highlight roll-off, slight green saturation) for Realistic look and Photo mode. Keep Neutral for editor swatches.
routes.species_coverage: All 26. Needs one reference photo set per species; all are common Ontario nursery stock that the owner can photograph.
routes.realism:
Colour is what a homeowner notices first. Over-bright, over-saturated or uniform greens read as CG at any distance. Today the live view (Neutral) and Photo mode (AgX) already render greens differently.

Anchors:
- Summer foliage linear albedo 0.09-0.12 (https://polycount.com/discussion/comment/2085603, community chart).
- Grass (0.105, 0.133, 0.041) (https://physicallybased.info/).
- About 15% reflectance at 550 nm (classic leaf-reflectance measurements, via search).
- Far Cry 3 calibration notes: https://blog.selfshadow.com/publications/s2012-shading-course/mcauley/s2012_pbs_farcry3_notes_v2.pdf.
routes.licence: Owner-made photos and scans: the owner owns them. No third-party licence; the chart is hardware.
routes.cost:
Runtime 0 ms, 0 bytes.

Hardware, which needs owner purchase approval:
- Calibrite ColorChecker Classic: US$74.25 on sale, US$99 list (https://calibrite.com/us/product/colorchecker-classic/).
- Optional flatbed scanner, Epson Perfection V39 II: US$129.99 MSRP (SHI listing, https://www.publicsector.shidirect.com/product/46113042/Epson-Perfection-V39II). Canadian prices vary; Walmart.ca listed C$327.28 (https://www.walmart.ca/en/c/kp/epson-scanner). Verify at Best Buy Canada.
routes.owner_actions:
1. Approve buying the chart (and scanner, if wanted).
2. Photograph 26 species with the chart.
3. Decide whether Realistic look and Photo mode get a photographic grade distinct from editor Neutral.
routes.web_fit: Data only. It feeds the albedo of the atlases (R4) and the grade constants in showcaseGrade.ts/photoGrade.ts.
routes.risks:
1. Phone-camera reference photos are already tone-mapped; use RAW or chart-normalised values.
2. Measurements of sunlit leaves include specular sheen. Use cross-polarised or overcast shots for albedo.
3. Colour honesty with swatches: keep Neutral for editor product colours.

routes.name: R7 Photo mode on the current WebGLPathTracer (three-gpu-pathtracer 0.0.27): fix and tune for foliage
routes.what:
Already present:
- MIS on, combining light and BSDF sampling.
- The sun as a circular RectAreaLight (MIS-sampled), plus HDRI environment importance sampling.
- bounces 5, transmissiveBounces 6, filterGlossyFactor 0.55, a 384-spp default, in-browser DenoiseMaterial and AgX.
- OIDN for batch stills outside the browser.

Changes:
(1) Remove the leaf emissive 'glow' (photoMaterials.ts:183-189, 422-436). It ignores shadow and position, so leaves glow in shade.
(2) Give leaves real light through them:
   (a) Quick: thin-wall transmission 0.1-0.25 (thickness 0 means isThinFilm, MaterialsTexture.js:329) at roughness about 0.6. Shadow rays then pass stochastically through leaves, tinted by albedo (attenuate_hit_function.glsl.js:125-147).
   (b) Correct: a roughly 50-line GLSL patch adding a Lambertian transmission lobe. Use cosine sampling about -N with pdf cos/π, applied when thin-film, transmission > 0 and roughness ≥ 0.5, so glass and water stay specular.
(3) transmissiveBounces 10-16. Alpha skips consume this budget, then real bounces (PhysicalPathTracingMaterial.js:464-465), and starved shadow rays count as blocked, which over-darkens dense canopies.
(4) Sun angular radius 0.265 deg.
(5) Raise textureSize to 2048 only for close-up stills.
(6) Limit baked LOD0 to plants in or near the frustum. bakeInstances merges every instance into world space.
routes.species_coverage: All 26. Transmission matters most for broadleaf species and grasses; alpha handling matters most for needle and scale species.
routes.realism:
With good assets this reaches archviz-still quality (Corona/V-Ray class) at Corner and Front:
- Real multi-bounce GI (green bounce, sky occlusion under canopies).
- Physically soft area-sun shadows and true contact shading.
- Light through leaves.

Limits:
- No true diffuse transmission without the patch: transmission colour equals reflection colour.
- Textures capped at 1024 (WebGLPathTracer.js:142).
- No instancing, so memory is high.
- Bed close-up and macro realism are capped by card leaves and the 1024 textures.

The repo has no vegetation demo; the examples are listed at https://raw.githubusercontent.com/gkjohnson/three-gpu-pathtracer/main/README.md.
routes.licence:
three-gpu-pathtracer, MIT (https://github.com/gkjohnson/three-gpu-pathtracer/blob/main/LICENSE; local node_modules copy): 'Permission is hereby granted, free of charge ... to deal in the Software without restriction, including without limitation the rights to use, copy, modify, merge, publish, distribute'. Patching the GLSL is allowed; keep the notice.

Open Image Denoise (batch path): Apache-2.0; the project says it 'is released under the permissive Apache 2.0 license' (https://github.com/RenderKit/oidn).
routes.cost:
$0 cash.

Per-sample time: transmissive bounces 10-16 add an estimated 10-30%. Diffuse transmission adds variance, so expect about 1.5x samples for equal noise (estimate). Keep the 384-spp default with OIDN.

Memory: about 70-100 B per triangle baked (estimate). At 2.52M triangles today that is about 0.2-0.25 GB; at 7M triangles of photoreal LOD0 about 0.5-0.7 GB, plus a CPU-side copy.

textureSize 2048: 16 MB per texture layer, and it applies to EVERY scene texture (house, pavers and so on).
routes.owner_actions:
1. Look sign-off: Photo mode loses its 'glow' and gains real backlight.
2. Decide whether photo stills may use LOD1 beyond about 60 ft to save memory.
routes.web_fit:
- Lazy tracer module, unchanged.
- A shader-chunk patch done like pcssShadows.ts (string replace on the tracer's GLSL before compile).
- Works in desktop Chrome, Edge and Safari via WebGL2.
- Phones: memory is risky above about 2M baked triangles (estimate).
routes.risks:
1. WebGLPathTracer was deprecated in 0.0.25 on 2026-09-28 and 'will be removed in a future release' (https://raw.githubusercontent.com/gkjohnson/three-gpu-pathtracer/main/CHANGELOG.md). Pin 0.0.27.

routes.name: R8 Photo mode on WebGPUPathTracer (three-gpu-pathtracer/webgpu) plus a diffuse-transmission patch
routes.what:
Port photoEngine.ts to the WebGPU tracer shipped in the same package. Per node_modules/three-gpu-pathtracer/src/webgpu and API.md it has:
- Per-instance BVH for InstancedMesh and BatchedMesh (PathtracerBVHComputeData.js:983-990, getBVH(object, instanceId)). No more bakeInstances; memory scales with unique species geometry.
- Native-resolution texture atlas pages (AtlasTexture.js, skyline packing) instead of 1024 layers.
- maxTransparentBounces 5, kept separate from maxBounces 15 so that, per its docs, foliage and cutouts cannot exhaust the bounce budget.
- An in-browser OIDNDenoiser (oidn-web, 'small' or 'large' weights), an FSRUpscaler, SunLight (0.0.27), and Sobol / blue-noise sampling.

The WGSL GltfCompliantMaterial also has no diffuse-transmission lobe; add one as in R7(b). Keep the WebGL tracer as the fallback.
routes.species_coverage: All 26. Instancing makes photoreal LOD0 for all 273 estate plants feasible in a still: 26 unique species meshes instead of 273 baked copies.
routes.realism:
Highest in-browser still quality:
- About 9/10 at Corner and Front with good assets.
- Leaf texture detail at native resolution for Bed close-up and macro.
- A clean OIDN result at modest sample counts, using albedo and normal guides (OIDN: auxiliary albedo and normal help preserve fine details, https://github.com/RenderKit/oidn).
routes.licence:
three-gpu-pathtracer MIT (quoted in R7).

The oidn-web weights come from the OIDN weights repository (Apache-2.0 per the OIDN project). Confirm the oidn-web package licence before adding it; not verified here.
routes.cost:
$0 cash.

- OIDN weights are an extra download whose size was not verified ('small' and 'large' variants exist).

GPU memory (estimate): about 26 species × about 25k triangles × about 80 B, roughly 50-60 MB of geometry, plus native-resolution atlases.

1. Approve a WebGPU-first Photo mode with WebGL fallback.
2. Approve the extra OIDN weights download, which happens only when Photo mode is used.
routes.web_fit:

routes.name: R9 Server-side offline Photo-mode stills (Blender Cycles on a rented GPU)
routes.what:
Photo mode posts the saved design JSON to a private render worker. The worker:
1. Rebuilds the scene in headless Blender from DeckCraft's data and private plant assets kept off the public repo.
2. Renders with Cycles: Translucent BSDF for leaves, unlimited instanced polygons, 4K textures, OIDN.
3. Returns a JPEG.

Only pixels reach the browser.
routes.species_coverage: Whatever asset library is licensed, which opens premium scan-based libraries that forbid browser distribution. All 26 species are coverable if the asset sweep finds them; coverage is decided by the sources sweeps.

routes.name: R10 Captured Gaussian-splat plants (Spark for three.js, or PlayCanvas SOG)
routes.what: The owner captures real specimens (phone video, then splat training) and places them as SplatMesh objects in DeckCraft's three.js scene via Spark. Spark is MIT and needs three r180+; it reads PLY/SPZ/SPLAT/KSPLAT/SOG (https://github.com/sparkjsdev/spark). Spark 2.0 LOD streaming was reported for April 2026 (https://radiancefields.com/platforms/spark).
routes.species_coverage: Any species the owner can capture. All 26 are common Ontario nursery stock, so coverage is feasible at species and even cultivar level.
routes.licence:
Spark: MIT (repo and radiancefields listing). Captures made by the owner are the owner's.

Terms of the training app (Postshot, Luma, Scaniverse) were NOT verified and must be checked before use.
routes.cost:
Bytes: about 10-25 MB per million splats in SOG (PlayCanvas: a 4M scene is about 42 MB, https://blog.playcanvas.com/playcanvas-open-sources-sog-format-for-gaussian-splatting/). A single plant at 0.2-1M splats is roughly 2-25 MB.

GPU: per-frame sorting cost. Heavy on phones.

Tool prices not verified.
routes.owner_actions:
1. Capture sessions (26 species).
2. Approve any paid training app or sign-up.
3. Decide whether a 'specimen viewer' outside the lit yard is acceptable.
routes.web_fit: Poor fit for the lit yard: no relighting, no shadows, no Photo-mode tracing, and large bytes per plant on phones. Best as a separate 'see the real plant' hero viewer from the species picker.
routes.risks:
1. Visible lighting mismatch beside relit geometry.
2. Sorting and overdraw cost.
3. Large downloads.
4. Capture quality varies (wind, background clean-up).

routes.name: R11 Cloud pixel streaming (Unreal Engine 5 / Twinmotion Cloud) as the live-realism ceiling
routes.what:
Rebuild the 3D view in Unreal (Lumen GI, Nanite; UE 5.7 Nanite Foliage is experimental) or Twinmotion, and stream the video to the browser.

Twinmotion Cloud presentations (https://dev.epicgames.com/documentation/en-us/twinmotion/an-overview-of-twinmotion-cloud):
- Pixel streaming at Ultra quality.
- Sessions capped at 60 minutes.
- Textures limited to 2K.
- Up to 100 concurrent viewers, then a queue.
- 4 GB per presentation.
routes.species_coverage: Whatever UE/Fab assets are licensed. Not limited by browser distribution, because assets stay on the server.
routes.realism: The highest live (interactive) realism: Epic claims realistic foliage at 60 FPS with Nanite Foliage (https://80.lv/articles/unreal-engine-5-7-is-now-availabe, experimental). Video compression artefacts and latency apply.
routes.licence: Pixels only reach the browser, so assets are never extractable. Engine and content EULAs (Unreal EULA, Fab) need their own review: Unreal EULA https://www.unrealengine.com/eula/publishing (not fetched here). Treat as UNVERIFIED.
routes.cost:
Streaming:
- Arcware Lite: €10/month + €0.15/min, 2 concurrent.
- Arcware Core: €89/month + up to €0.10/min (https://arcware.com/pricing/).
- Vagon Streams: $0.025-0.047/min by GPU, plus $0.67/day per app (https://vagon.io/streams/pricing).
- Twinmotion seat: about $445/year (secondary source, https://visualizee.ai/blog/twinmotion-pricing).

A 15-minute homeowner session costs about €1.50-2.25 (Arcware Lite) or $0.38-0.71 (Vagon).

Engineering: a full rewrite of DeckCraft's 3D. Months.
routes.owner_actions:
1. Sign-ups and a metered spend cap.
2. A strategic decision to abandon the in-browser renderer.
3. Accept per-minute cost per visitor.
routes.web_fit: Zero download, but needs a good connection. Latency on cellular phones, queueing at peaks, no offline use.
routes.risks:
1. Cost scales with traffic.
2. A complete rewrite.
3. Mobile latency.
4. Vendor lock-in.
Recommended only as a reference ceiling, not as a plan.

routes.name: R12 Live renderer migration to three.js WebGPURenderer: TRAA, SSGI, screen-space contact shadows, custom MSAA resolve
routes.what:
three r185 already ships these TSL post nodes (node_modules/three/examples/jsm/tsl/display):
- TRAANode (temporal reprojection AA).
- SSGINode (screen-space GI after SSRT3).
- SSSNode (screen-space contact shadows: shadow maps for the foundation, SSS for detail).
- GTAONode, DenoiseNode, TAAUNode.
- ImportanceSampledEnvironment, adapted from three-gpu-pathtracer.
An SSGI example exists (https://threejs.org/examples/webgpu_postprocessing_ssgi.html).

WebGPU also allows a tone-mapped MSAA resolve. WebGL2 cannot, since it has no multisample textures.
routes.realism:
Moves the desktop live view toward a still render:
- Green bounce and sky occlusion under canopies (SSGI).
- Leaf-level contact shadows (SSS).
- No shimmer while moving (TRAA).
- Correct leaf edges against the sky.

About +1 point over R1-R5 on desktop. Little benefit on phones, where the cost is too high.
routes.licence: three.js MIT (quoted in R1). The SSGINode cites SSRT3 as a reference (https://github.com/cdrinmatane/SSRT3); that is a technique reference, not a dependency.
routes.cost:
$0 cash.

Engineering: large. Every onBeforeCompile and ShaderChunk patch (foliageLighting, pcssShadows, surface, sky and water shaders) must be rewritten in TSL, and GTAOPass, UnrealBloom and SMAA swapped for node equivalents.

GPU: SSGI is typically several ms at full resolution (unmeasured); run it at half resolution and on desktop only.
routes.owner_actions: A strategic go or no-go on the renderer migration. It changes the whole 3D view, not just plants.
routes.web_fit: WebGPURenderer falls back to a WebGL2 backend automatically (https://threejs.org/manual/en/webgpurenderer). Tier-gate SSGI and TRAA to high. The bundle-size impact on the 340 KB viewer chunk needs measuring.
routes.risks:
1. Biggest rewrite risk of all the routes.
2. TSL APIs change between releases.
3. TRAA ghosting with frameloop='demand'.
4. CI SwiftShader has no WebGPU, so tests stay on the WebGL backend.
